en: Having approached the exceedingly beautiful shore of the Ocean of Milk— which is praised by Brahmā, Mahendra, Surendra, the hosts of Maruts, Rudra, and the lords of sages— he who is the noble protector of the virtuous;
then, for the sake of alleviating the burden of the earth, he manifested his form as the dense mass of consciousness, whose fame was already celebrated.
O descendant of Raghu, O cloud of compassion, grant to me, who worships you, the service of your lotus feet. || 1 ||

O lotus-petal-eyed one, O ornament of the Raghu dynasty, O compassionate Lord, O you whose body is as dark as a cloudless blue water-lily, O Sun who illumines the lotuses of the hearts of all the worlds! O one of tender limbs, O beloved of Gautama, purified by the particles of dust from your holy lotus-feet!
O descendant of Raghu, O cloud of compassion, grant to me, who worships you, the service of your lotus feet. || 2 ||

O Pūrṇa, O Supreme beyond the supreme, protect me, who am exceedingly wretched and without a protector; O infinite ocean of bliss, O Rāma, whose yellow upper garment is as enchanting as a lightning flash in a monsoon cloud, salutations to you!
O destroyer of desire, O one with a most beautiful face, O you adorned with golden ornaments and a jeweled crown!
O descendant of Raghu, you who are a mass of compassion, grant to me, who worships you, the service of your lotus feet. || 3 ||
O Lord with a magnificent crown of large pearls as radiant as the divine autumn moon,
whose splendor is like ten million suns, who are purified by your beautiful conduct, holding a wondrous bow and arrow in hand;
you who have shattered the great elephant-like trunk of the Rākṣasa king with your fierce and mighty staff-like arms!
O descendant of Raghu, you who are a mass of compassion, grant to me, who worships you, the service of your lotus feet. || 4 ||

O Rāma, today out of compassion, lift me up from this ocean of worldly existence, which is filled with thousands of serpents that are the afflictions and fierce poisons, which is staked by the great fires of divine wrath, which consists of waves of birth, old age, and death, which is teeming with crocodiles and whirlpools of pride and passion, and which is a long-fallen pit of suffering.
O descendant of Raghu, you who are a mass of compassion, grant to me, who worships you, the service of your lotus feet. || 5 ||

Swiftly liberate the one who is deluded, miserable, helpless, wretched, and has come for refuge— his mouth compressed by the clouds of thirst and hunger like a fierce elephant intoxicated by the madness of saṃsāra, crushed by the staff-like arms [of karma], and afflicted by passion and darkness while abandoned by the state of ecstatic delusion.
O descendant of Raghu, you who are a mass of compassion, grant to me, who worships you, the service of your lotus feet.

O Raghuvīra, you who are steadfast in great battle, compassion toward me— whose intellect is exceedingly dull and whose heart-lotus is fallen, filled with the sins accumulated over hundreds of births and resembling that of a beast—
is fitting; for you, O merciful one, are my mother, sister, and father, as well as my protector.
O descendant of Raghu, you who are a mass of compassion, grant to me, who worships you, the service of your lotus feet. || 7 ||

O Rāma, having abandoned you— who are compassionate, affectionate toward the destitute, a necklace of blue lotuses, boundless, and noble— whom else, O Lord, should I go for refuge, unless it be one who is free from affliction?
Therefore, O God, may I always joyfully take shelter at your lotus feet along with Sītā.
O descendant of Raghu, you who are a mass of compassion, grant to me, who worships you, the service of your lotus feet. 8.

This eight-verse hymn, which removes all that is undesirable, belongs to that foremost of the Raghus— who is an ocean of the nectar of compassion, a supreme kinsman to those who are protectorless, a performer of the highest deeds, a boat for the waves of fear of his devotees, and one who delights in beautiful excursions upon the banks of the Sarayū river; whoever [recites it]...
That mortal who recites this obtains the service of the lotus feet of Acyuta-Rāma.
Thus ends the *Śrīsītārāmāṣṭaka*, composed by the ascetic Acyuta, disciple of the venerable Madhusūdanāśrama.
